items.title: Jack Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997

ctx.x: Well the band broke up at The Famous Door. We went to The Famous Door and it was around Christmas time — what a time to be let go, right? And the two bosses, Mutt and Jeff we called them because one was a big guy and the other one was shorty. They decided they couldn’t afford to have the band during the Christmas holidays. So they let the band, the big band go, and they just kept Red Norvo and Mildred Bailey, and three other musicians. And John Kirby’s quintet was the alternate band. So that was it. So there I…
Well in addition to all this big band playing, I know you’ve done a lot of small group things back in Rome? You’ve done your share of circus music, which is pretty strenuous, isn’t it?
